acceptance: TPCHThroughputTest receives the adapter's target dialect and passes it to every get_query call (pre-generation and fallback)
A test asserts that for each throughput-capable platform, throughput stream SQL equals the power-path SQL for the same query, seed and stream parameters
stream_id is passed in the form get_query actually reads, with a test
The DuckDB real-database throughput test still passes
context: 2026-10-04 throughput adversarial review (develop 8ed0c64e1). Consensus finding from two reviewers; confirmed by script.
description:
`TPCHThroughputTest` calls `benchmark.get_query(...)` without `dialect=` (benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py:259-264 and :307-312), and `execution.py:474-480` does not pass one. With no dialect, `tpch/benchmark.py:384-387` makes the target equal to the source (netezza). The power path passes `dialect=adapter.get_target_dialect()` (platform_power.py:114,141; power_test.py:289-295). TPC-DS throughput already passes the dialect (execution.py:340). The `stream_id=` keyword is also ignored by get_query, which reads only `params["stream_id"]`.

A reviewer compared all 22 queries with and without a dialect: they differ for duckdb, spark, mysql, doris, singlestore, sqlite and questdb; only postgres is identical. This is the root cause of the SQLite `INTERVAL '1 YEAR'` failures, and likely breaks Doris, SingleStore and QuestDB throughput. On DuckDB it means power and throughput time different SQL text, so the phases are not comparable.

This is a generic defect; the SQLite item covers only the SQLite symptom and connection model.
